Maintenance Report — MNT-0127-002

Asset: WELL-0127 (NE-07 Well 127, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 28 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 07 Feb 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 254 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0127-0015 on 2023-01-26 Report written: 08 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0127-0015 showed the wellhead at 11.7 °C with the air at 10.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly922
Bolts, shims and seals231
Bearing grease and consumables384
Labour (company crew and contractor)1,576
Total3,113

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0127-008

Asset: WELL-0127 (NE-07 Well 127, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: separator Work started: 30 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 10 Jan 2024 19:00 · Well stopped for this job: 275 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0127-0061 on 2023-12-28 Report written: 11 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0127-0061 showed the wellhead at 7.1 °C with the air at 5.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0127-015

Asset: WELL-0127 (NE-07 Well 127, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 07 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 08 Mar 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 17 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0127-0122 on 2025-03-06 Report written: 09 Mar 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0127-0122 at 11:30 on 2025-03-06 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.0% of the pad area, estimated 2.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.0 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 378 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 302 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0127-015 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.51% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Asset: WELL-0127 (NE-07 Well 127, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 16 May 2025 08:00 · Finished: 17 May 2025 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 22 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0127-0132 at 14:30 on 2025-05-15 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.7 hours after the inspection. External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0127-025

Asset: WELL-0127 (NE-07 Well 127, T350, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 28 Jun 2026 08:00 · Finished: 15 Jul 2026 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 407 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0127-0190 on 2026-06-25 Report written: 17 Jul 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0127-0190 showed the wellhead at 40.3 °C with the air at 32.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
